sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Writ Petition No.29063 of 2021
Order:

This writ petition is filed with the following prayer:
"to issue writ or direction more particularly in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondent Nos.2 to 4 illegally executed sale deed as per petitioner sale deed vide Doc.No.4757/2016 and patta pass books in favour of the Respondent No 7 instead of petitioners name without following due process of law as highly illegal arbitrary unjust unconstitutional and violation of principles of natural justice and also in violation of Articles 14, 21 and Article 300-A of the Constitution of India and consequently to direct the Respondent Nos.2 to 4 make enquiry into the matter as per sale deed and delete the name of Respondent No 7 after due enquiry and confirm petitioner title and possession as per sale deed and issue the New patta pass book in favour of the petitioner land admeasuring Ac.0-35 guntas in Survey Nos.15/U, Ac.0-35 guntas in Survey No.15/UU and Survey No.15/EE Ac.0-25, total Ac 215 guntas situated at Marepally Village Thimmajipeta Mandal, Nagarkurnool District by virtue of registered sale deed vide Doc.No.4757 of 2016, dated 23 09 2016 pending disposal of the above writ petition"

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the un-official respondents and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4.
3.

When the matter is taken up for consideration, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has initiated civil proceedings vide O.S.No.230 of 2017 on the file of learned Junior Civil Judge, Nagarkurnool.

It is further submitted that the petitioner is the bonafide purchaser and is in possession of property located in Survey No.15/U admeasuring Ac.0-35 guntas, Survey No.15/UU admeasuring Ac.0-35 guntas and Survey No.15/EE admeasuring Ac.0-25 guntas situated at Marepally Village, Timmajipeta Mandal, Nagarkurnool District, by virtue of a registered sale deed dearing document No.4757 of 2016, dated 23.09.2016, and accordingly had approached the official respondent - Revenue Divisional Officer for mutation proceedings.

However, vide, the impugned proceedings, the respondent No.3, through letter No.M/2614/2019, dated 13.11.2019, and addressed a communication to respondent No.4, directing deletion of the names of legal heirs of Smt.Shoba Rani, W/o.Shankaraiah, from the records of Survey No.15.

It was stated therein that the subject land had already been acquired under Kalvakurthy Lift Irrigation Scheme (for short "KLIS"), and that compensation had been received by Smt. Shoba Rani from her father-in-law, late Thirupathaih, on Sri.Doma Venkataiah vs The State Of Telangana on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48156484/
1 01.06.2007 under proper acknowledgement.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the very question arises as to whether the said letter dated 13.11.2019, purportedly based on the acts of Smt. Shoba Rani, can be sustained in the eye of law, in as much as there is nothing to record to establish that Smt. Shoba Rani was ever vested with lawful authority to receive compensation in respect of the land which had already been gifted by late Thirupathaiah in favor of his granddaughters.
Though Smt. Shoba Rani was the daughter-in-law and mother of the minor children, she did not possession legal capacity to alienate or to receive compensation with respect to subject property.

The petitioner, after verifying the legal title of the original owners, purchased the subject property through a registered sale deed and thereafter filed necessary applications before the revenue authorities seeking mutation of his name in the revenue records.

However, the official respondents, without considering the petitioner's request or affording him an opportunity of hearing, proceeded to record the land as acquired under the Kalvakurthy Lift Irrigation Scheme, on the basis of the alleged receipt of compensation of Smt.
Shoba Rani.
Such action is arbitrary, illegal and contrary to law.
Accordingly, the petitioner prays this Court to allow the writ petition in the interest of justice.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue would submit the name of KLIS has been entered in the revenue records upon thorough verification and upon enquiry, it was found that the land had been gifted by one Thirupathaiah in favor of his granddaughters.
It is further submitted that the said land was acquired by the Government in the year 2006 itself, and compensation was duly paid as required under law for acquiring the subject property.
The petitioner, however, claims title under a sale deed bearing document No.4757 of 2016, registered before the Office of the Sub- Registrar, Achampet Mandal.

It is contended that the land was acquired vide proceedings No.A3/415/2005, dated 13.12.2006, issued by the Special Collector (Land Acquisition), Bheema Project, Mahabubnagar, wherein compensation of Rs.2,65,000/- was paid to the original landlord,
Thirupathaiah.
Thereafter, the name of KLIS was entered in the revenue records.
Subsequently, in a partition, an extent of Ac.2-25 guntas fell to the share of Smt.Shoba Rani and Ac.1- 32 guntas to the share of Thirupathaiah.

Later, Thirupathaiah repaid an amount of Rs.1,57,000/-, which he received towards land compensation in respect of Ac.2-25 guntas in Survey No.15 of Marepally Village,
Thimmajipeta Mandal, to Shoba Rani.
Consequently, Shoba Rani issued a statement declaring that she had no land in Survey No.15 of Marepally Village and raised no objection for deletion of her name.
Accordingly, the petitioners' names were deleted from the records.

It is further submitted that the petitioner's purchase of Ac.2-15 guntas from Smt. Shaoba Rani, mother of minors by name Vikas, Vipula and Vijaya, under registered document No.4757 of 2016, dated 23.09.2016, has no legal basis, as the land had already been acquired by the Government and the name of KLIS has been entered in the revenue records.
Therefore, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

5. Learned counsel for un-official respondent Nos.5 and 6 adopted the same contention, asserting that they had purchased the land from the original landlord, Thirupathaiah and that without issuing notice to them, their names were not entered in the revenue records.
They contend that pattadar passbooks have already been issued in their favor and hence prayed for dismissal of the writ petition.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, un-official respondent Nos.5 and 6 and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue, and upon perusal of the record, this Court Sri.Doma Venkataiah vs The State Of Telangana on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48156484/
2 noticed that land belonged to three persons namely Vikas, Vipula and Vijaya, represented by their mother Smt. Shoba Rani, which had already been acquired by paying compensation, and a no-objection letter issued.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the entire extent of Ac.7-35 guntas in Survey No.15 of Marepally Village, Thimmajipet Mandal, was acquired, and the name of KLIS has been entered in the revenue records.

The question that arises is whether the consent letter issued by the land owners can be treated as valid acquisition in terms of the Land Acquisition Act, without following the procedure prescribed thereunder.
The issue is required to be examined by the respondents in consultation with the Land Acquisition authorities.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to file an application before the revenue authorities, who, in turn, shall issue notice to all concerned parties,
including the official respondents, and pass appropriate orders strictly accordance with law.
7. In so far as the rival claims of the petitioner and un-official respondents over the subject property are concerned, this Court refrains from making any observations.
The parties are at liberty to work out their remedies before the competent Civil Court, provided the land is released from acquisition by the Official respondents.
8. For the aforesaid reasons, the claim of the petitioner as well as un-official respondents does not hold any sustainability in the eye of law.
9. Accordingly, with the above observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
